shows.title: Shadow of a Doubt
shows.artist: Antonio López, Barbara Goldmann, Chaeheun Park, Jean-François Lauda, Michael Kennedy Costa, Minh Lan Tran, Mona Welch, Wilson Miller
shows.description: A group show curated by Bill Cournoyer that borrows its title from Hitchcock's 1943 thriller about a charming uncle who may be a murderer. The eight artists, including Antonio López, Chaeheun Park and Mona Welch, deal in images that look calm and ordinary but carry a note of unease. Domestic scenes, portraits and still lifes sit side by side, and the pleasure of the show is in the small dislocations: something slightly off in a familiar room, a gaze that lasts a beat too long.

shows.title: Gelitin Mirrors
shows.description: The Viennese collective Gelitin, known for anarchic performances and collaborative installations that blur the line between artwork and audience, take over MASSIMODECARLO Pièce Unique, the single-window space on rue de Turenne, with a show about mirrors. Their rambling, playful text runs from obsidian mirrors of 6200 BC through the magic and vanity mirrors of ancient cultures, and the works themselves are handmade, lumpy and funny, showing the work and the viewer at once. A short run, through November 7.

shows.title: library house
shows.description: Ian Kiaer has shown with Marcelle Alix since the gallery's early days, and library house continues his long-running way of working in fragments. The London artist builds modest, precise arrangements from found materials, inflatables, paper, foam and small paintings, each one a model or proposal for an idea about architecture and how we live in space. The show takes its cue from Jean-Christophe Bailly's essay about libraries that can never contain the world, and Kiaer's quiet installations feel like notes toward a building that could never quite be completed.

shows.title: Solitude and Silence
shows.description: Skarstedt's avenue Matignon gallery pairs two artists who were friends in surrealist Paris in the early 1930s: the sculptor Alberto Giacometti and the painter Yves Tanguy. Giacometti's busts of his brother Diego and his elongated, eroded figures share the room with Tanguy's dreamlike plains scattered with smooth, bone-like forms under endless skies. Both artists made work about isolation and the space around a single figure or object, and placing them together brings out an eerie quiet in each.

shows.title: Bloom in the Sunlight, Dream in the Moonlight
shows.description: Rosana Paulino has spent her career asking what it means to be a Black woman in Brazil, using drawing, printmaking, sewing and installation to work through the country's colonial and scientific archives. Her new show at Mendes Wood DM's Place des Vosges gallery comes out of more than a decade of research into spirituality and feminine power, imagining goddess figures that are part woman, part plant, part myth. The works are lush and botanical, with roots and tendrils growing from bodies, and offer a counter-image to the violence that runs through much of her earlier work.

shows.title: Sperlonga 1959
shows.description: In the summer of 1959 Cy Twombly spent time in Sperlonga, a fishing village south of Rome, and made a group of drawings that became one of the turning points of his career. Galerie Karsten Greve, Twombly's longtime dealer, gathers a rare body of these works on paper in the Marais: pencil, crayon and paint marks that scatter, cluster and erase themselves across the sheet, already looking like the graffiti-like writing of his later paintings. Small and fragile, they are a chance to see the moment his language came together.

shows.title: Jardin d'amour
shows.description: A group show curated by Guillaume Logé, named after his new book, that ranges from so-called Arts Premiers to contemporary work around two linked ideas, nature and love. Jeanne Bucher Jaeger has championed artists with ecological and humanist concerns for more than a century, and the show draws on that history: a Fernand Léger ink drawing of a woman with a rose sits near Yang Jiechang's ten-panel silk painting Tale of the Eleventh Day. The underlying question is whether love, in an age of apps and fractured relationships, might be reinvented by opening up to the living world.

shows.title: Ubiquitous Conjunction
shows.description: Kunié Sugiura moved from Japan to Chicago in 1963 to study at the School of the Art Institute, found photography there and has lived in New York since 1967. Her first show at galerie frank elbaz, curated by the critic Ryo Sawayama after last year's SFMOMA survey, spans her career: photo-paintings that print photographic emulsion straight onto canvas next to acrylic, darkroom photograms of plants and animals, and works like Christmas Lights (1979) that join different times and places on one surface. She was mixing photography and painting decades before it became common.

shows.title: Waiting for the Sound of Thunder
shows.description: The Viennese artist Jakob Lena Knebl takes over Loevenbruck's space at 12 rue Jacques-Callot with one of her immersive installations. Knebl treats the history of art and design as raw material to cut up and recombine, mixing furniture, textiles, mannequins, color and found objects into environments that are sensual, funny and openly about desire. Her rooms invite viewers in rather than keeping them at a distance, and they ask how identity is built in the space between people and the things they live with.

shows.title: Pascal Convert
shows.description: Pascal Convert's first solo show in Christophe Gaillard's Paris space centers on glass, a material he has worked with for years, alongside photography, sculpture and film. Convert's work is steeped in memory and history, and here his text evokes the legend of glass born from fire and sand on a tidal shore, and the deep red that glassmakers call the blood of Christians. The pieces are luminous and elegiac, objects that seem to hold time inside them. The gallery hosted a conversation between Convert and the philosopher Georges Didi-Huberman during the show.

shows.title: A Canadian Season
shows.artist: Manuel Mathieu, Kapwani Kiwanga, Larissa Fassler
shows.description: Galerie Poggi turns to the Canadian art scene with three solo presentations under one roof. Manuel Mathieu, the Haitian-Canadian painter, has his first solo show in France with Ayizan, abstract canvases thick with memory and ritual. Kapwani Kiwanga, the Paris-based Canadian artist who represented Canada at Venice in 2024, shows sculptural works that examine power through materials and color. Larissa Fassler presents a short retrospective of her intricate drawn maps of city squares and transit hubs, built from hours of on-site observation.

shows.title: Vivre Sa Vie
shows.description: In 1996 Rita Ackermann staged Vivre sa Vie once, a live puppet performance that mixed underground music, experimental film and fashion with collaborators from the New York downtown scene. Galerie Allen brings that seminal, rarely seen project back as an exhibition, gathering the puppets, drawings, film and ephemera that survive from it. It is a window onto the Hungarian-born painter's early years, when her girlish, punk drawings were everywhere in the zines and music videos of the moment, and it shows the roots of the layered, erased paintings she makes today.

venue.name: Galerie Allen
venue.address: 6, passage Sainte-Avoye, entrée par le, 8 Rue Rambuteau

shows.title: Pomodoro & Sottsass. A Friendship Seen by Ugo Mulas
shows.artist: Arnaldo Pomodoro, Ettore Sottsass, Ugo Mulas
shows.description: For the centenary of Arnaldo Pomodoro's birth, Tornabuoni Art's avenue Matignon gallery brings together the sculptor and the designer Ettore Sottsass through the eyes of the photographer Ugo Mulas, who documented both men and the lively Milan art world after the war. Pomodoro's cracked, gleaming bronze spheres and columns sit beside Sottsass's enamels and ceramics, with Mulas's black-and-white photographs of studios and foundries tying the story together. It is a portrait of a friendship and of a city that reinvented Italian art and design.

shows.title: Silhouettes
shows.description: Charles Fréger is known for his series of portraits of people in uniform and costume, from Alpine wild-man carnival figures to Indian folk performers, shot frontally and with great formal rigor. Silhouettes, at Les filles du calvaire's rue Chapon space, gathers images from several of these series, including his photographs of Alsatian wedding costume. Fréger's subjects become almost sculptural, defined by their outlines and the traditions they wear. The gallery closes for the holidays from December 21 to January 4.

shows.title: Entre temps
shows.description: Fresh from a big show at the Grand Palais, Leandro Erlich brings his installation Classroom to France for the first time, at Xippas in the Marais in partnership with Galleria Continua. The Argentine artist is famous for illusions built from everyday architecture, swimming pools you can stand under and building façades you seem to climb. Classroom is a schoolroom seen through glass in which visitors find their own reflections sitting at the desks like ghosts, a simple, unsettling trick about memory and presence.

shows.title: Inertia
shows.description: Nino Kapanadze's first solo show at Michel Rein gathers the images, forms and questions that have run through the French-Georgian painter's work for several years along a single path. Her new paintings sit between abstraction and figuration, with faint figures, interiors and landscapes surfacing from washes of color and then sinking back. The title points to the stillness the canvases cultivate: they feel suspended, as if time had slowed down long enough for a half-remembered image to be held in place.

shows.title: The Home I Have Never Had
shows.description: Amoako Boafo's fourth solo show with Mariane Ibrahim is staged as a domestic interior in the gallery's avenue Matignon space. The Ghanaian painter is known for portraits of Black subjects whose skin he paints with his fingers in swirling, textured strokes, set against flat, bright grounds and patterned clothes. Here new paintings hang alongside earlier studies from 2017, and the idea of home, one he says he never had, frames them as an imagined family of friends and sitters gathered in one place.

shows.title: Une histoire chuchotée de l'art
shows.description: Peter Freeman's small gallery in the Palais-Royal arcades devotes a show to Robert Filliou, the Fluxus poet-artist who argued that art is what makes life more interesting than art. The selection runs from Hand Show, a 1967 box of silkscreened hand portraits made with Scott Hyde, to the Galerie légitime, a gallery Filliou carried around in his hat, plus telegrams, wordplay and objects that treat art as a game. Its title, A whispered history of art, suits a body of work that is light, generous and quietly radical.

shows.title: Kreëmart : Provocateurs de la consommation expérimentale
shows.description: Kreëmart, the production studio founded by Raphaël Castoriano, has spent two decades inviting artists to make edible or consumable works, from cakes and sweets to performances built around food. Galerie Alberta Pane surveys its most important collaborations with international artists, with documentation, objects and new pieces that test what happens when art is meant to be eaten and disappears. It is a playful show about appetite, pleasure and the economy of art, held in the gallery's Marais space.

shows.title: Nothing to Read
shows.artist: Jean-Michel Basquiat, Irma Blank, Alighiero Boetti, Betty Danon, Mirtha Dermisache, On Kawara, Jiří Kolář, Michael Krebber, Glenn Ligon, Henri Michaux, Roman Opałka, Mimmo Rotella, Gary Simmons, Christopher Wool
shows.description: A group show at Mitterrand's rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré gallery about writing that cannot quite be read. Irma Blank's and Mirtha Dermisache's asemic scripts, Henri Michaux's ink signs, Roman Opałka's counting paintings and On Kawara's date paintings sit with Christopher Wool's stenciled words, Glenn Ligon's smeared text, Basquiat's crossed-out lists and Boetti's embroidered alphabets. Fourteen artists treat letters and marks as image, rhythm and gesture, and the show makes a strong case that the most expressive writing can be the kind you cannot decode.

shows.title: La Jalousie
shows.description: For her second show with Emanuela Campoli, the Italian artist Anna Franceschini takes her title from Alain Robbe-Grillet's novel, where jalousie means both jealousy and the slatted window blind through which a husband spies on his wife. Franceschini's films and kinetic sculptures play with the same idea of seeing and concealing: her camera slides behind and around objects such as shop mannequins and window displays, animating things that are usually still and making ordinary commercial spaces feel strange and almost magical.

shows.title: Evoke the line
shows.description: The Korean artist Nam Tchun-Mo builds his work out of a single element, the line. In his best-known pieces, strips of canvas or steel are bent into repeating U-shaped channels that rise off the wall and catch light and shadow, recalling furrowed fields and the strokes of Chinese characters. This selection of recent works at Ceysson & Bénétière's rue du Renard space shows how much variety he draws from that one gesture, in vivid reds, blues and whites that change as you move around them.

shows.title: In Your Pocket
shows.description: Inès Longevial's fourth show at Ketabi Bourdet is built around pocket-sized paintings: canvases small enough to hold in one hand, accumulated in her studio over four years. Known for warm, sunlit portraits of women with flushed faces and flowers, Longevial shrinks the format until the paintings become personal objects you approach like a phone screen rather than a picture on the wall. Hung in quantity in the passage Dauphine gallery, they read like a diary of glances, gestures and moments of light.

shows.title: Fast asleep in a room somewhere
shows.description: The young Italian painter Leonardo Devito shows new oil-and-acrylic paintings at Ciaccia Levi's nomadic space on rue Meslay, with a text by the Pompidou curator Annalisa Rimmaudo. Devito paints in a soft, dreamlike register: celestial guardians, signs and street corners from his native Turin appear as if half-remembered on waking, in hazy blues and dusky pinks. The title fits the mood, a sequence of images that feel like they come from someone sleeping in another room.

shows.title: Court of Public Opinion
shows.artist: Eyrie Alzate, Ursula Bradley, Nicolas Ceccaldi, Billy Coulthurst, Antoinette Demonceaux, Albert Dietrich, Hana Earles, Ian Miller, Catherine Österberg & Jacques Rogers, Matthew Pang, Moritz Smid, Maria Toumazou, Lena Tutunjian & Ed Lehan, Bob van der Wal, Alex Vivian, Mike Kelley, Cindy Sherman
shows.description: A sprawling group show organized with the artists Matthew Pang and Moritz Smid and the platform TOTO, gathering a loose network of younger artists, many from Melbourne, London and Vienna, around two older guests, Mike Kelley and Cindy Sherman. The works are raw, funny and confrontational, from Alex Vivian's paintings on filthy bedsheets to Nicolas Ceccaldi's dark assemblages, and the title hints at the court of social media where reputations are made and broken. It is messy in the best sense, a snapshot of a scene rather than a thesis.

shows.title: Théâtre des possibles - Le masque dans tous ses états
shows.artist: Yasmina Benabderrahmane, Benoit Huot, Smaïl Kanouté, Esmeralda Kosmatopoulos, Dmitry Kostyukov, Shiva Lynn Burgos, Peter Lökös, Sebastian Riemer, Yang Yi, Julien Vignikin
shows.description: A group show at Galerie Dix9 on the mask in all its forms. Whether it hides, reveals or transforms, the mask lets people do and be what ordinary life does not allow, and the artists here take it in many directions: Smaïl Kanouté's painted and danced bodies, Yasmina Benabderrahmane's photographs, Benoit Huot's costumed totems, Yang Yi's and Julien Vignikin's portraits. Photography, sculpture and painting share the walls, and the show plays between carnival, ritual and the everyday masks of social life.

shows.title: Saul Steinberg
shows.description: Galerie Claude Bernard, which showed Saul Steinberg in his lifetime, brings together drawings and collages by the Romanian-born American artist best known for his New Yorker covers. The show includes the famous kind of image that made him a household name, such as the 1976 still-life cover, alongside The American Sphinx and works like Eastern Federal Savings and Loan Association (1978) that send up American architecture, money and bureaucracy. Steinberg's line is witty, precise and endlessly inventive, and these sheets show why artists admired him as much as magazine readers did.

shows.title: Du silence à la parole / From Silence to Voice
shows.artist: Brognon Rollin, Joseph Grigely, Guerrilla Girls, Suzy Lake, Allen Ruppersberg, Martha Wilson
shows.description: mfc-michèle didier, a gallery and publisher devoted to artists' books and editions, looks at the passage from silence to speech. Brognon Rollin, this year's winners of the Prix Marcel Duchamp, show 24h Silence, a 1950s jukebox that plays only silence; Joseph Grigely, who is deaf, shows the paper notes from his written conversations; and the Guerrilla Girls, Suzy Lake, Allen Ruppersberg and Martha Wilson bring works about who gets heard. It is a small, thoughtful show in which words, and their absence, carry political weight.

shows.title: Stuck
shows.description: Phung-Tien Phan, a German artist of Vietnamese descent, makes deadpan sculptures, videos and installations from the stuff of family life and consumer culture: kitchen furniture, children's toys, plastic bags and home-movie footage. Her show at Edouard Montassut's small space in the 9th arrondissement is called Stuck, and the works feel suspended between domestic comfort and quiet frustration, funny and a little sad at once. She makes the overlooked routines of migrant and middle-class households into something worth looking at closely.

shows.title: The Sugars at the Bottom
shows.description: The American painter Chaz Guest shows new work at RX&SLAG's Paris gallery on rue des Quatre-Fils. Guest paints figures with loose, expressive brushwork, often drawing on music and on Black American history and family life, and the title, The Sugars at the Bottom, evokes the sweetness that settles at the bottom of a glass. The paintings are warm and layered, built from memory and storytelling as much as from observation.

shows.title: b(EYE)rth r(EYE)ght
shows.description: The Atlanta-based painter and scholar Fahamu Pecou returns to Backslash with new paintings. Pecou is known for large, bold portraits of young Black men, often posed with swagger and painted in a mix of hip-hop imagery and art-historical references, that challenge stereotypes about Black masculinity. The punning title, birthright with an eye in it, points to vision, inheritance and the right to be seen on one's own terms.

shows.title: Adieu La Famille
shows.description: Galerie PACT, a small space on rue des Gravilliers open into the evening, shows new work by the French painter Amélie Bigard under the title Adieu La Famille, Goodbye to the Family. The gallery keeps its texts short; the show is a chance to see a younger painter in one of the Marais's more adventurous rooms, open Wednesday to Saturday until 9pm.

shows.title: Alone together
shows.description: Milène Sanchez's second solo show in Claire Gastaud's Paris space on rue Chapon brings new paintings made with oil glazes, a technique going back to the early Renaissance. They grew out of a trip to New York to see the women of Abstract Expressionism, Joan Mitchell, Lee Krasner, Helen Frankenthaler and Elaine de Kooning, and they carry some of that energy into thin, luminous layers of color where faces and figures surface and fade.

shows.title: Legendary Lines
shows.description: Part of a year Galerie Danysz is devoting to urban art, Legendary Lines sets pioneers of 1980s New York graffiti, such as Dondi White, beside more recent artists. Rather than retelling the movement's history, it follows a single thread: the line, the signature stroke that made a writer recognizable at a glance and was passed on from crew to crew. The title plays on all its meanings, from a painted line to a career sustained over decades and the lineage between generations.

shows.title: Les Diachroniques
shows.description: Galerie Binome, devoted to photography and its extensions, presents Les Diachroniques, a show built around time and change. It includes Laurence Aegerter's Lithophanies, in which her images of haystacks, a nod to Monet's series, are cast in thin porcelain that reveals the picture only when light passes through it. The works play with how images shift with time and light, and how a photograph can become an object.

shows.title: Lucky Jim
shows.description: At 97, the Ghanaian photographer James Barnor is still surprising people. His third show at Galerie Clémentine de la Féronnière on the Île Saint-Louis draws previously unseen prints from his archive around one theme, the self-portrait and the way he staged himself. Barnor's career runs from studio portraits in pre-independence Accra to swinging-sixties London for Drum magazine and back, and these images show the humor and mischief behind the camera as well as the elegance of his sitters.

shows.title: Park Chan-wook
shows.description: Galerie VU', the photography gallery in the 15th, shows the still photographs of the South Korean filmmaker Park Chan-wook, director of Oldboy and The Handmaiden, as part of the PhotoSaintGermain festival. Park has photographed for decades alongside his film work, and his images share the precise framing and strange, quiet tension of his movies, but on a smaller, more personal scale.

shows.title: Sete
shows.description: The Italian painter Pietro Moretti shows new paintings at Romero Paprocki in the Marais under the title Sete, Italian for thirst. Moretti works in oil with a loose, gestural hand, building scenes in which figures and landscape blur into one another in rich, saturated color.

shows.title: (Nice Dream)
shows.description: Alexandre Yang's first solo show in Paris takes its title from Radiohead's 1990s song and its theme too: a dreamer imagines being at the center of everyone's affection, cherished and adored, while in reality remaining alone inside the reverie. Yang paints meticulous, slightly uncanny autofictional scenes in which he appears among friends and family, and the precision of the painting makes the loneliness underneath it all the sharper.

venue.name: Galerie Marguo
venue.address: 4 rue des Minimes, Entrée (entrance):, 35 Rue des Tournelles

shows.title: Du Domaine des Mères
shows.description: Jean-Claude Silbermann, one of the last artists to have taken part in André Breton's surrealist group, is still working in his nineties. At Galerie Sator he shows cut-out paintings on shaped plywood, figures he calls Dames, which try to catch the presence of the Mothers, the mysterious powers Mephistopheles describes to Faust as the source of all forms. The works are colorful, witty and strange, part emblem, part puppet, part dream image. The critic Philippe Dagen talks with the artist at the gallery on Saturday, November 7, at 4pm.

shows.title: Riding Hot
shows.description: Santiago de Paoli's third show with Galerie Jocelyn Wolff spreads across two Paris venues, the gallery's space on rue de Penthièvre near Matignon and Abraham & Wolff. The Argentine painter makes small, sensual paintings of bodies and animal-like forms in shades of red and flesh, suggestive without being explicit, painted on burlap and rough grounds. They are intimate and physical, built up slowly, and they reward close looking.

shows.title: Anish Kapoor
shows.description: Since the late 1970s Anish Kapoor has kept asking the same question: how can matter produce immateriality? At Mennour's space at 6 rue du Pont de Lodi he answers with works spanning nearly thirty years, from Non Object (Sphere) of 1998 and concave-convex mirrors that swallow and flip the room, to the twisting Bridge Twist, the dark Namibia paintings and new untitled pieces from 2026. It is a compact survey of an artist who makes surfaces disappear.

shows.title: The Wind, the Earth and the Fire
shows.description: Yinka Shonibare's first solo exhibition in Paris, at Mennour's 5 rue du Pont de Lodi space, brings together the elements of the title through his signature Dutch wax-print patterns. There are bronze wind sculptures that look like billowing printed fabric, Earth Pictures of endangered lemurs, a Refugee Astronaut, and new Nature Works about gas flaring in Nigeria. As always, the British-Nigerian artist uses those colonial-era textiles to talk about trade, identity and, here, the ecological cost of extraction.

shows.title: L'insaisissable nature du réel
shows.artist: Jean Arp, Constantin Brancusi, Alberto Burri, Lucio Fontana, Sam Francis, Helen Frankenthaler, Alberto Giacometti, Yves Klein, Lee Ufan, Joan Miró, Louise Nevelson, Judit Reigl, Germaine Richier, Günther Uecker, Maria Helena Vieira da Silva, Manoucher Yektai
shows.description: Mennour's avenue Matignon gallery stages a museum-grade group show of postwar masters around one idea: that reality never lets itself be fully grasped, and slips away the moment we think we understand it. Brancusi, Giacometti and Germaine Richier, Fontana's slashes and Burri's burns, Klein's blue, Frankenthaler's stains, Nevelson's shadow boxes and Lee Ufan's quiet marks each find a different way to make form feel unstable or open. It is a rare chance to see this many blue-chip works side by side outside a museum.

shows.title: Let There Be
shows.description: Brooklin A. Soumahoro shows a new series of Window paintings at Mennour's original Saint-Germain gallery on rue Saint-André-des-Arts. Each canvas is built from overlapping fields and bands of color, coded in the titles by their hues, that read like light falling through a pane or the frame of a window onto another space. The paintings are spare and luminous, and the title, Let There Be, gives them the feel of a first light.

shows.title: dottore di tutto #3
shows.description: christian berst's second space, the bridge, devotes its third monographic show to Giovanni Bosco (1948–2009), a former Sicilian shepherd who became one of the most inventive figures of art brut. About a dozen unseen works show his fierce visual vocabulary of hearts, robots, little homunculi and blocks of poetic text, painted on cardboard and paper and once covering the walls of Castellammare del Golfo. Few of his works still circulate, which makes this a rare look.

shows.title: À l'intérieur
shows.description: For the bicentenary of photography and the centenary of Michel Foucault's birth, christian berst gave the curator Marc Donnadieu carte blanche in its main gallery. À l'intérieur is a show about confinement that sets works made in asylums, prisons and other closed places beside documentary and historical photographs of those institutions. It is moving and unsettling, a look at how creativity survives inside walls and at the gaze that watched over those inside.

shows.title: Godspeed You Black Emperor
shows.description: Ladji Diaby's show at Crèvecœur's original space on rue des Cascades in Belleville borrows its title from the Canadian post-rock band. Diaby, a young Paris artist, works across painting, photography and assemblage, and the show is moody and atmospheric, with dark, layered surfaces and images that feel like fragments of a soundtrack.

shows.title: Waiting as Time Shifts
shows.description: The Japanese painter Daisuke Fukunaga fills Crèvecœur's rue de Beaune galleries in Saint-Germain with new paintings of everyday workers and quiet moments, from people resting to figures absorbed in routine tasks, rendered in soft, glowing color with a dreamlike blur. Waiting as Time Shifts suits work that slows down ordinary scenes until they feel suspended.

shows.title: Hygiène de l'art. Contre culture
shows.description: Parliament teams up with Galeria Plan B, the gallery of Cluj and Berlin, for a joint presentation in its Marais space. The title borrows Jean Dubuffet's polemic against 'cultural asphyxia' and frames a show about art made against the grain of official culture, with works from the two galleries' programs.

shows.title: Alchemy
shows.description: Almine Rech's first monographic show of Robert Indiana, organized with the Robert Indiana Legacy Initiative, takes its title from a line he wrote in 1961 about turning junk into art and the neglected into the wanted. The show goes beyond LOVE, the image that made him famous, to the assemblages he built from beams and scrap found around his Coenties Slip studio in Lower Manhattan and the bold, stenciled word-and-number paintings of the Pop years. During Art Basel Paris a monumental LOVE WALL was also installed in the city as part of the fair's public program.

shows.title: Le mur vert bouteille
shows.description: The Danish artist Maria Zahle shows new wall works at Galerie Maria Lund in the Marais. Zahle makes hybrid objects between painting and sculpture, stretching dyed and painted fabric over shaped wooden frames so that color, texture and depth all become part of the surface. The bottle-green wall of the title sets the tone for a show about color as a physical, almost architectural presence.

shows.title: Gardens
shows.description: Osama Al Rayyan, born in Damascus in 1995 and now based in Basel, shows new paintings at Galerie Sultana. He paints without tying himself to fixed references, letting personal memories and art history seep into each other, and he prefers experiment to explanation. His canvases work with subtle contrasts of color and soft, layered forms in which gardens, figures and interiors seem to drift in and out of focus.

shows.title: Shahrazad / شهرزاد
shows.description: The Palestinian artist Aysha E Arar takes Scheherazade, the storyteller of the Arabian Nights who saves women's lives by telling stories, as the guiding figure of her show at Sans titre. Arar works in charcoal, acrylic and pastel on long lengths of fabric, rubbing in leaves and dust, and the large hanging pieces read like scrolls or tents. They carry fragments of dialogue and figures that seem half-dreamed, a quiet meditation on storytelling as survival.

shows.title: rose pour toi, rose pour moi
shows.description: Pierre et Gilles mark fifty years together with about twenty portraits made over the last two years, shown at Templon's rue Beaubourg gallery alongside a new monograph, Five Decades. Since meeting in 1976, the photographer Pierre Commoy and the painter Gilles Blanchard have fused their crafts on single images: staged photographs that Gilles then paints over, producing saturated, idealized portraits of friends, performers and models dressed as saints, sailors and gods. Kitsch, tender and meticulously made, their pictures have become an instantly recognizable part of Paris culture.

shows.title: Brisure
shows.description: Gérard Garouste, one of France's most important living painters, unveils paintings, drawings and sculptures made over the past four years at Templon's rue du Grenier Saint-Lazare space. Breaking is at the heart of this body of work: for Garouste, to break is to interrupt a form that has grown too settled and to crack open fixed readings, of images and of texts. His crowded, twisting figures draw as ever on the Bible, the Talmud and literature, here around themes such as the Tree of Life, the Sephiroth and the Tower of Babel.

shows.title: L'Essence du portrait
shows.description: Ropac's Marais gallery looks at Irving Penn as a portraitist, from his early, existential picture of Marcel Duchamp to an exultant Elizabeth Peyton photographed in the last decade of his life. Penn helped lift photography to the status of high art, and his portraits, often set against a bare backdrop or squeezed into a narrow corner, rival paintings in technical bravura and psychological weight. The show coincides with Penn & Fashion at the Maison Européenne de la Photographie.

shows.title: Mémoires sédimentaires
shows.description: The Moroccan artist Mouhcine Rahaoui, a 2017 graduate of the Tetouan School of Fine Arts, returns to AFIKARIS for his second solo show. His work is rooted in Jerada, his hometown in Morocco's Oriental region, and in the experience and history of its miners, in a town where survival often means taking dangerous risks underground. The new paintings, such as La chute du ciel, mix personal memory with that raw reality in dark, layered surfaces lit by flashes of light.

shows.title: Catacaos
shows.description: The Venetian-Peruvian photographer and sculptor Lorenzo Vitturi found his subject in Catacaos, a small town in northern Peru overflowing with poto, the dried calabash gourds sold in every shop and market stall. His new body of work, at 193 Gallery, follows that fascination into photographs, sculptures and assemblages that play with the gourd's curving forms and its role in local craft and daily life, mixing documentary and collage in his signature colorful way.

shows.title: to those who see in the dark
shows.description: The Palestinian artist and filmmaker Noor Abed's first solo exhibition in France, at Galerie Imane Farès, includes her new film we walk in our sleep (2026), under the title to those who see in the dark. The opening on Saturday, November 7, 3–8pm, includes a conversation between Noor Abed and the artist Saodat Ismailova at 6pm.

shows.title: Le Sortilège
shows.description: For his first solo show at Galerie Anne Barrault, Bertrand Dezoteux presents a set of watercolors and a new film, Le Sortilège, which blends animation and live action to tell a decisive moment in the life of Rémi Pitoys, a driving instructor who seems to have been bewitched. Dezoteux has a gift for gentle, absurd fictions, and the show plays with the rules of the road, blind spots and mirrors as a metaphor for how we make sense of the world.

shows.title: La dernière plage
shows.description: For her first solo show at Les filles du calvaire, the French photographer Marie Quéau fills the ground floor of the gallery's historic space with unseen work from her series Le Royaume and FURY. In both she looks at bodies at tipping points, in training, in combat or in crowds, where the lines between fiction and reality, control and abandon, the individual and the group start to blur. Opening reception Thursday, November 12, 6–9pm; closed December 21 to January 4.

shows.title: Patria Nostra
shows.description: Julie Joubert's first solo show, upstairs at Les filles du calvaire, is the result of three years embedded with the French Foreign Legion. The series Patria Nostra won the public prize of the Prix Découverte Fondation Louis Roederer at the Rencontres d'Arles, and its photographs look closely at the men, rituals and bodies of an institution that is famously closed to outsiders. Opening reception Thursday, November 12, 6–9pm.

shows.title: Têtebêche
shows.description: In Adrien Chevalley's studio in Vevey, some books never make it to the shelf: they lie on tables among sketches, molds and prototypes, wrapped in new covers he has drawn himself to make them his own. The Swiss artist's show at Semiose grows from that habit of borrowing and kinship with other authors, in sculptures, ceramics and drawings that turn familiar objects head to tail, as the title suggests.

shows.title: Guten Morgen Sonnenschein
shows.description: Juergen Teller's new show at Galerie Suzanne Tarasieve in the Marais brings new photographs by the German photographer who made his name with raw, flash-lit fashion and celebrity pictures that look like snapshots. His recent work mixes commissions, travel and family, including The Prada Coat No. 11, made in Kaunas in 2026, and the title, Good Morning Sunshine, promises his usual mix of humor and candor.

shows.title: Gilles Aillaud
shows.description: Loevenbruck devotes its space at 12 rue Jacques-Callot to Gilles Aillaud (1928–2005), the painter of Narrative Figuration best known for his cool, detached pictures of animals in zoos: hippos, snakes and big cats behind bars and glass, painted as a quiet critique of captivity and of the way society looks at and controls. The show includes Serpent (1964). Opening reception Thursday, December 10, 6–9pm.

shows.title: et les sentinelles de la joie
shows.description: Virginie Barré opens a new solo show, et les sentinelles de la joie, at Loevenbruck's 6 rue Jacques-Callot space. The picture shows her recent exhibition Absolue de rose at the Espace de l'Art Concret in Mouans-Sartoux; the gallery has not yet posted views of the Paris show. Opening reception Thursday, December 10, 6–9pm.

shows.title: Entre deux rives
shows.description: Loeve&Co, the Saint-Germain gallery known for avant-garde and Lettrist art, presents Frédérique Devaux Yahi, a filmmaker and artist of the experimental cinema scene, in a show curated by Frédéric Acquaviva. Entre deux rives, Between two shores, looks at her work across film, images and writing, and at the two sides of the Mediterranean in her history. Opening reception Wednesday, November 4, from 6pm; the gallery closes November 17–29.

shows.title: Strip
shows.description: Les Douches la Galerie, a photography gallery in the Marais, shows Rebekka Deubner's series Strip (2022–2023), introduced by Julie Héraut of Le BAL. Deubner photographs fragments of clothing and fabric up close, a yellow strap on a glowing red-orange ground, worn seams and loose threads, so that the garments become intimate, almost bodily images about undressing, wear and what fabric remembers.

shows.title: Je veux qu'elles restent
shows.description: Victoria Palacios's first solo show in Paris, at Nathalie Obadia's Cloître Saint-Merri galleries, brings nearly fifty new works. The French artist, based in Brussels, is also a musician and performer, and her paintings work like stages, crowded with figures, costumes, props and materials, so that it is hard to tell whether we are watching the beginning of a performance, its climax or its last scene.

shows.title: Runaway Ground
shows.description: The American painter Jason Saager's second Paris show with Nathalie Obadia, at the Faubourg Saint-Honoré gallery, continues his long exploration of landscape. Roads wind between hills and lead nowhere, hills recede into unknown distances and clouds settle on the land, all painted with a pictorial sleight of hand that makes the scenes feel both familiar and impossible.

shows.title: Impact
shows.description: Wang Yancheng, the Chinese-born abstract painter who has lived in Paris since the 1980s, shows new canvases at Lelong's rue de Téhéran gallery after a run of honors abroad, including a 2025 exhibition in the Galleria dell'Accademia in Florence, steps from Michelangelo's David. His large paintings explode with poured and splashed color, energy and light, at the meeting point of Chinese ink painting and Western lyrical abstraction.

shows.title: Ovals
shows.description: After My Best, an alphabet of twenty-six small wooden pieces shown at Lelong in 2023, Richard Tuttle returns, this time to the avenue Matignon space, with Ovals, a large series of watercolors. As always with Tuttle, the work follows a precise, self-imposed program, and the constraints produce endless, delicate variations: modest means, a light hand and a sense of discovery in every sheet.

shows.title: Dans chaque coquillage il y a le noir de la mer
shows.description: Gaëlle Chotard's show at Galerie Papillon takes its cue from Agnès Varda's line that if you opened her up you would find beaches. Chotard makes delicate drawings and sculptures in thread, wire and ink that evoke sandy shores, shells and the deep sea, forms that hold the traces of what has passed through them. The title, In every seashell there is the blackness of the sea, sets the mood: fragile, precise work about depth and memory. Opening reception Saturday, November 7, 3–8pm.

shows.title: European Couples
shows.description: Gagosian's vast hangar-like gallery at Le Bourget airfield, just north of Paris, hosts a long-running show of Dan Flavin's fluorescent light works under the title European Couples. Flavin built his art entirely from off-the-shelf fluorescent tubes and fixtures, arranging them in corners, barriers and grids so that colored light floods and reshapes the space around them, and the scale of Le Bourget lets the light fill an entire architecture. The show runs into April.

shows.title: Paul Rebeyrolle
shows.description: For the centenary of Paul Rebeyrolle's birth, Galerie Claude Bernard mounts his first Paris show in fifteen years: about ten paintings from 1989 to 2004 drawn from three late series, Le Monétarisme, Clones and Implosions. Rebeyrolle was one of the great figurative painters of the 20th century, and his work is violent, rebellious and politically engaged, with the anger carried by the sheer physical matter of the paint: thick impasto, collaged materials, bodies and banknotes torn into the surface.

shows.title: Chroniques de la mer et d'une tempête
shows.description: Miguel Rothschild's fifth solo show at Bendana | Pinel reads the sea and the sky as chronicles, witnesses to a time that resists being pictured, with the storm as both weather and a state of tension. In works such as Cumulonimbus and Undercurrents, the Argentine-born, Berlin-based artist prints photographs on reflective surfaces and then works into them with charcoal, so the light seems to burst from the image as you move in front of it. The opening is Saturday, November 7, from 4pm.

shows.title: Lot Bò D'lo A (The Other Side of the Water)
shows.description: The Haitian-American painter Didier William shows new work at Peter Kilchmann's Marais space. William builds his figures from thousands of carved and inked eyes, so bodies seem to look back at the viewer, and he draws on Haitian history, migration and Vodou. The title, the other side of the water, points to diaspora and the crossing between Haiti and elsewhere.

shows.title: Beginnings
shows.description: Zander Galerie Paris shows Tina Barney's early black-and-white photographs, rarely seen pictures she rediscovered in her archives during the pandemic. Long before the large color portraits that made her name, Barney was already photographing the private world of East Coast families in the late 1970s, with the same intimacy and attention to gesture. Opening reception Thursday, November 5, 6–9pm.

shows.title: Back in Black
shows.artist: Pilar Albarracín, Arman, Hans Bellmer, Ben, Pol Bury, Marcel Duchamp, Aube Elléouët, Valentine Hugo, Tetsumi Kudo, Georges Mathieu, Roberto Matta, Henri Michaux, Jacques Villeglé and others
shows.description: About twenty works from the 20th century to the 2000s, all built around black, used less as a color than as a mood, a material or a void. Galerie 1900-2000, a Saint-Germain specialist in Dada and Surrealism, mixes Duchamp, Bellmer, Michaux and Matta with Arman's smashed glasses, Tetsumi Kudo's strange boxes and younger artists.

shows.title: What the water kept : Ce que l'eau a gardé
shows.description: Salon 94 inaugurates its new Paris gallery in the Palais-Royal gardens with Deborah Roberts. The Texas artist makes collages of Black children assembled from cut photographs, painted fragments and mismatched features, images that look at how Black childhood is seen, policed and idealized.

shows.title: Portraits
shows.artist: Pablo Picasso, Joan Miró, Salvador Dalí, Marc Chagall, Jean Dubuffet and others
shows.description: Mayoral's avenue Matignon space looks at the portrait as self-reflection, projection and experiment, from ancient coins to dissolving 20th-century figures. The show gathers Picasso, Miró, Dalí, Chagall and Dubuffet with younger artists such as Marria Pratts.

shows.title: I paint time.
shows.description: About twenty works by Sam Francis from 1950 to 1980 at A&R Fleury on avenue Matignon. The Californian painter, who lived in Paris in the 1950s, built his canvases from luminous splashes and pools of color around open white space.

shows.title: Héritages vivants. Réinventer les formes
shows.description: Galerie Christophe Person pairs the Congolese artist Raymond Tsham and the Mozambican ceramist Reinata Sadimba, whose works ask how stories, crafts and symbols travel through time and feed identity today. Sadimba's hand-built clay figures and Tsham's mixed-media works sit side by side.

shows.title: La première période de ma peinture, c'est l'amour...
shows.description: Galerie Pavec looks at Maurice Denis, a leader of the Nabis, through the early paintings he made of his wife Marthe and their family, a period he later summed up as love. Tender, decorative and full of quiet domestic scenes, the works show the painter at his most personal.

shows.title: Inner Sky
shows.description: Pavec devotes a show to Jacqueline Lamba (1910–1993), the surrealist painter long overshadowed by her marriage to André Breton, with works from 1969 to 1980 from the estate kept by her daughter Aube Breton-Elléouët. Her late paintings dissolve towns, rivers and clouds into vibrating color.

shows.title: Opsine
shows.description: The French painter Eva Nielsen shows new paintings at The Pill on Place de Valois, alongside her place in the Marmottan's survey of landscape from Monet to Hockney. Nielsen layers oil, acrylic and screenprint on canvas and organza, so her landscapes shimmer between photograph and painting.

shows.title: Talent (1986/2026)
shows.description: Isabella Ritter, with The Green Gallery of Milwaukee, restages David Robbins's Talent, his 1986 grid of professional headshots of his artist friends, from Cindy Sherman to Jeff Koons, made with a Broadway headshot photographer. Forty years on, it still reads as a sharp joke about art-world celebrity.

shows.title: Hommage à Jean Fournier
shows.description: Ahead of its 80th anniversary in January 2027, Galerie Dina Vierny pays tribute to Jean Fournier, the dealer who championed Parisian abstraction from 1964 to 2006 and whose gallery closed for good in 2024. The show gathers works by artists from his program at the gallery's rue de Seine space.

shows.title: Pegeen
shows.description: DURAZZO presents Pegeen (1925–1967), the daughter of Peggy Guggenheim and Laurence Vail, whose naïve, dreamlike paintings of women, children and painters at work were long overshadowed by her family. It is described by the gallery as the first exhibition of its kind in Paris.

shows.title: Rocket Science
shows.artist: Robert Cumming, Steven Pippin, Roman Signer
shows.description: Three artists who turn the scientific experiment into deadpan comedy: Robert Cumming's staged photographs of absurd contraptions, Steven Pippin's cameras made from toilets and washing machines, and Roman Signer's small explosions and flying objects. A smart, funny show at Jean-Kenta Gauthier's gallery in the 15th.

shows.title: Leonor Fini
shows.description: Galerie Minsky, the Leonor Fini specialists, show paintings, watercolors and drawings by the Argentine-Italian surrealist (1907–1996). Fini's sphinxes, witches, cats and androgynous women are theatrical, erotic and strange, and she was one of the most independent women of the Paris avant-garde.

shows.title: L'Orange
shows.description: The American painter Richard Aldrich shows new work at Modern Art's Paris space on Place de l'Alma. Aldrich makes loose, diaristic abstract paintings in which drips, scraps of canvas and stray marks carry as much weight as composition.

shows.title: Giorgio Morandi. Un luogo dell'infinito
shows.artist: Giorgio Morandi, Josef Albers, Lucio Fontana, Ettore Spalletti, Lee Ufan
shows.description: Galleria Maggiore's Paris space sets Giorgio Morandi's quiet still lifes of bottles and boxes in dialogue with Josef Albers, Lucio Fontana, Ettore Spalletti and Lee Ufan, artists who also found the infinite in a few simple forms and colors.

shows.title: La mort du cygne
shows.description: Good or Trash, a young gallery on the Canal Saint-Martin, shows the Paris-based artist Sarah Benslimane under the title The Death of the Swan. The gallery is open Wednesday to Saturday afternoons.

shows.title: Zurbarán 1598–1664
shows.description: The Louvre's big autumn show is a full retrospective of Francisco de Zurbarán, the painter of Spain's Golden Age whose monks, saints and still lifes emerge from deep darkness with an almost sculptural stillness. It gathers loans from Madrid, Seville and collections worldwide.

shows.title: Contemporary Counterpoint: Vija Celmins
shows.description: The Orangerie's contemporary counterpoint series sets Vija Celmins's meticulous night skies, ocean surfaces and spiderwebs, drawn and painted over months, beside Monet's Water Lilies. Two ways of losing yourself in an endless surface.

shows.title: Le chaos-monde 1918–1948
shows.description: The Musée Picasso surveys Kurt Schwitters, the Dada artist who built his Merz collages and assemblages from tickets, labels and scraps of the street, and kept reinventing his art through exile in Norway and England until his death in 1948.

shows.title: Toi et ta bande
shows.description: A group show at the Palais de Tokyo gathering artists and collectives working outside the big cities, in rural and small-town France, where art is made with friends, neighbors and local communities. Part of the museum's autumn season, which also includes shows by Ali Cherri, Sonia Gomes and Valérie John.

shows.title: Histories of Landscape: From Monet to Hockney (1890–2026)
shows.description: The Marmottan and the Musée de Grenoble trace landscape painting from 1890 to today, from Monet's late gardens to David Hockney, with artists such as Eva Nielsen bringing the story up to the present.

shows.title: The Harvest Season
shows.description: The Ghanaian artist Ibrahim Mahama fills the Fondation Cartier's new building on Place du Palais-Royal with his vast installations of jute sacks, salvaged materials and the traces of labor and trade. The Fondation holds a late opening on Friday, November 6, 7–10pm.

shows.title: Gustave Fayet: Collector – Designer. Icons of Modern Art
shows.artist: Gustave Fayet, Vincent van Gogh, Paul Gauguin, Odilon Redon and others
shows.description: The Fondation Louis Vuitton tells the story of Gustave Fayet, the early 20th-century collector who bought Van Gogh, Gauguin and Cézanne before almost anyone else and designed carpets and furniture himself, with masterpieces from his collection, including Van Gogh's self-portrait with bandaged ear.

shows.title: Penn & Fashion
shows.description: The MEP pays tribute to Irving Penn (1917–2009) through his fashion photography for Vogue, from Balenciaga and Dior to Issey Miyake, images whose spare backdrops and sculptural poses changed how fashion was photographed. It pairs well with Penn's portraits at Ropac Marais.

venue.name: MEP – Maison Européenne de la Photographie

shows.title: Parallax
shows.description: The Jeu de Paume surveys the Canadian artist Stan Douglas, whose staged photographs and films restage overlooked moments of history, from a 1955 Vancouver racetrack crowd to riots and uprisings, with the precision of a film set.

shows.title: “I Spend My Life Painting”: Claude Monet
shows.description: A Claude Monet itinerary through the Musée d'Orsay's Impressionist gallery, following the painter from early works such as La Pie (The Magpie) to his late series, drawn from the museum's own collection.

shows.title: Towards a Sea
shows.description: Lafayette Anticipations presents the first institutional solo show in France of the Japanese painter Yu Nishimura, whose hazy, dreamlike figures and landscapes seem to dissolve into soft light.

shows.title: A Song for Europe
shows.description: The Swedish photographer Annika Elisabeth von Hausswolff's second solo show at the Paris gallery. She is known for carefully staged images with the cool look of documentary and crime-scene photography, which she turns on patriarchy, capitalism and the subconscious.

shows.title: Chuta Kimura: Peintures, pastels, dessins
shows.description: Le Minotaure's fourth show of Chuta Kimura, the Japanese painter of the second School of Paris who arrived in the city in 1953 at 36 with no money or contacts and built a career of vivid, energetic landscapes in paint, pastel and drawing.

venue.name: The Minotaur Gallery
venue.address: 2 Rue des Beaux Arts, 23 Rue de Seine

shows.title: À l'instant T
shows.description: Galerie Lahumière, long devoted to geometric abstraction, shows a photographer for the first time: Serge Najjar, born in Beirut in 1973, whose shots of real buildings and streets are framed into crisp geometric compositions that look almost abstract.

shows.title: Hommage à Pierre Daix
shows.description: A tribute to Pierre Daix (1922–2014), the journalist, writer and art historian who wrote the Picasso catalogue raisonné, through works by the artists he championed and befriended, including Hans Hartung.

shows.title: Can't Find Water
shows.description: The New Zealand artist Kate Newby makes small, tactile interventions from fired clay, glass, wire and found materials that change how you notice the floor, windows and corners of a room.

shows.title: Ce qui demeure
shows.artist: Núria Güell, Dominique Mathieu, Gianni Pettena, Matthieu Saladin, Endre Tót, les gens d'Uterpan, The Play, Lois Weinberger
shows.description: A group show for Salle Principale's tenth year, gathering the gallery's artists around what remains: traces, gestures and the politics of everyday spaces, from Lois Weinberger's photographs of plants to Endre Tót's conceptual works.

shows.title: Like a punch to the guts
shows.artist: Keunmin Lee, Shahryar Nashat, Steve Reinke, James Richards, Sibylle Ruppert, Diane Severin Nguyen
shows.description: A group show curated by Anya Harrison about images and objects that hit the body like a blow, with Sibylle Ruppert's dark surrealist drawings, video by Steve Reinke, James Richards and Diane Severin Nguyen, and work by Shahryar Nashat and Keunmin Lee.

shows.title: If You Don't Come In, Smile As You Go By, No. 2
shows.description: Ruttkowski;68's third show of Jårg Geismar (1958–2019), who painted cigarette-pack cellophane, glass shards and scrap wood with luminous glass paint and pinned them to the wall, alongside his quick drawings of people at train stations.

shows.title: Finally, a Good Exhibition
shows.description: The designer Stefan Sagmeister, who paints over unsold 19th-century canvases from his family's antique shop, in dialogue with the German sculptor Meuser, who has welded scrapyard steel into sculpture since the 1970s. A follow-on to Sagmeister's show at the Gaîté Lyrique.

shows.title: Dreaming of the Pirate's Sex
shows.description: The Portuguese artist Odete's show at Goswell Road, built around a poetic text about drifting at night and trying to find the way home, supported by the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation in France. Open Thursday to Saturday, 2–6pm, or by appointment.

shows.title: Mental
shows.description: The first European solo show of the New York painter Shane Rossi (b. 1995), with new paintings following his spring show at Ramiken.

shows.title: What Slips By
shows.description: New paintings by the Japanese artist Tomona Matsukawa about what goes unspoken between people: a silence at dinner, the space between two pillows. She starts by interviewing women about their lives and often titles works with their own words.

shows.title: L'Abstraction en passage
shows.description: Bailly's Paris gallery traces modern art's passage toward abstraction, with works by masters such as Marc Chagall.

shows.title: Anthropiques
shows.description: New paintings by Yann Lacroix, whose luminous, hazy landscapes mix overgrown gardens, pools and architecture, places where nature and human traces blur together.

shows.title: Aussi longtemps que les mirages
shows.description: A solo show of Katarzyna Wiesiolek, whose soft, dreamlike images of coastlines, seas and skies seem to hover between memory and mirage.

shows.title: On aurait pu se rencontrer
shows.description: Elias Loudiyi's first solo show at the gallery is about memory and loss. Working from family albums and photographs taken in France and Morocco, he paints imagined meetings between familiar faces and strangers, leaving empty spaces so the stories stay open.

shows.title: Immersion
shows.description: Polka's second Immersion show, part exhibition and part film, takes you behind Steve McCurry's camera after the gallery's director spent three days with him in Pennsylvania in September 2026.

shows.title: Les Ruines de Détroit, 20 ans après
shows.description: Twenty years after they began photographing Detroit's abandoned theaters, hotels and factories, Yves Marchand and Romain Meffre return to their famous series.

shows.title: Une nouvelle chambre à soi
shows.artist: Chiara Indelicato, Eloïse Labarbe-Lafon, Lili Lévy-Lajeunesse, Laura Makabresku and Sayo Senoo
shows.description: A group show of five women photographers taking their cue from Virginia Woolf's A Room of One's Own.

shows.title: Land and Sky
shows.description: Paintings by Sylvia Kanytjupai Ken, the Aboriginal artist from the APY Lands of South Australia, whose dense, rhythmic canvases carry the stories of her country across land and sky.

shows.title: En Levko
shows.description: A solo show of Dana Cojbuc at Catherine Putman's new address on rue Saint-Martin, on the corner of rue Chapon.

shows.title: Entre la chaîne et la trame
shows.artist: Jim Lambie, Danielle Orchard, Katherine Bradford, David Shrigley and others
shows.description: A group show about weaving and textile, from Jim Lambie's wool paintings and Katherine Bradford's woven painting to works by Danielle Orchard, HyeGyeong Choi, Sarah Dwyer, Rebecca Purdum and David Shrigley.

shows.title: WHY?
shows.description: The German painter Tatjana Doll turns brands, consumer goods, vehicles and political symbols into huge, fast, physical paintings.

shows.title: Timbre in the Current
shows.description: New sculpted paper works by Nate Lewis, shown at once in Paris and Luxembourg. Trained as a nurse, Lewis cuts and carves photographs and paper into textures that recall cells, tissue and topography.

shows.title: Hommage à Gilles Caron
shows.artist: Gilles Caron, with Diane Arbus, Brassaï, Henri Cartier-Bresson, Zanele Muholi and others
shows.description: For photography's bicentenary, a tribute to the war and news photographer Gilles Caron (1939–1970), from Jane Birkin on a film set to the Six-Day War, Vietnam and Northern Ireland, alongside Diane Arbus, Brassaï, Cartier-Bresson and Zanele Muholi.

shows.title: Que vos pas soient légers, car vous marchez sur mes rêves
shows.description: The Iranian photographer Payram's third solo show at the gallery, made with Polaroids, silver prints, solarized prints and collage, explores exile, refuge and memory. He left Iran after the 1979 revolution.

shows.title: Une épopée singulière
shows.description: New paintings by Gaëtan Vaguelsy, who keeps painting his circle of friends until the intimate portraits turn into a kind of epic.

shows.title: Remember Me
shows.artist: Irving Penn, Raymond Depardon, Nan Goldin, Cindy Sherman, Wolfgang Tillmans and others
shows.description: For photography's bicentenary, the Pinault Collection fills the Bourse de Commerce with about 700 photographs by more than 70 artists, from Gustave Le Gray and Dorothea Lange to Cindy Sherman and Wolfgang Tillmans, hung with no chronology. It includes nearly 450 Irving Penn photographs in "The World According to Penn" (until Jan 10), Raymond Depardon's La France (until Jan 25) and Nan Goldin's film Stendhal Syndrome. Free late opening the first Saturday of each month, 5–9pm.

shows.title: The History of Tears
shows.description: Barbara Kruger takes over Tadao Ando's Rotunda and the 24 display cases of the Passage with a flood of words, quotes from Orwell's 1984 and Aimé Césaire, filmed sequences and sound, turning the museum's center into one of her immersive text environments.

shows.title: FEAR: Art in the Age of Anxiety
shows.artist: Georg Baselitz, Joseph Beuys, VALIE EXPORT, Harun Farocki, Ron Mueck, Arnulf Rainer, Daniel Richter, Niki de Saint Phalle, Günther Uecker and others
shows.description: A large group show in Ropac's Pantin halls about art made in a climate of fear and anxiety, from Niki de Saint Phalle's shooting paintings and Beuys to VALIE EXPORT's organ pipes turned into missiles, Ron Mueck, Daniel Richter, Mandy El-Sayegh and Günther Uecker.

shows.title: Polla Series 2026
shows.description: New works by Prabhavathi Meppayil, the Bangalore artist from a family of goldsmiths, whose near-monochrome panels are inlaid with fine copper and gold wire and marked with goldsmiths' tools.

shows.title: Talia Chetrit
shows.description: A solo show of the New York photographer Talia Chetrit (b. 1982), whose staged portraits and self-portraits probe what stays hidden in how photographs get made. Tramps hasn't posted pictures of the show, so these are recent installation views of her work from her gallery Sies + Höke.

shows.title: Les Vestiges indociles
shows.description: Léonard Bourgois Beaulieu photographed stone at the Villa Medici in 2012, then let his negatives decay and change over time until they became living material. The gallery hasn't posted pictures of the show, so these are from his recent series Espa.èces menacé.es, Polaroids altered by nature in Venice.

shows.title: Photographier l'action
shows.artist: Günter Brus, Hannah Collins, Emo de Medeiros, John Goto, Nicola Lo Calzo, Chantal Regnault, Sue Williamson
shows.description: A group show on how photography records, and becomes part of, performance, from Günter Brus's 1970 action on rue de Vienne to contemporary rituals in Benin. The gallery has posted only portraits of the artists, so this picture comes from the show's public listing.
